bullets.text: The US has announced sanctions intended to "squash" Iran's economy, with the Treasury Secretary stating that allies must decide if they are "with us or against us."
A boat capsized in north-western Nigeria, resulting in dozens of deaths, with many of the victims feared to be children.
More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine collapsed due to a landslide in the Central African Republic, and the death toll is expected to rise.
Police are investigating a fatal fire at a caravan park in Melbourne, where a person died early this morning. A crime scene has been established in Campbellfield.

A High Court decision to admit a secret recording of a man admitting to raping his wife could pave the way for victims of serious crimes to use similar recordings as evidence. Family lawyers believe this opens new avenues for justice.
Farmers and conservationists in Queensland are united in their opposition to the state parliament's critical minerals bill, calling for its repeal after it was passed without amendments.
US long-term bonds experienced a slide, with the yield on 30-year Treasuries rising, despite the US Treasury's efforts to increase purchases of securities to soothe investors.
Investors are reducing their bets on interest rate rises in the US and UK, influenced by weaker economic data, even as oil prices have seen a rally.
A key regional price benchmark for aluminum delivered to the US market declined after indications that the Trump administration would lower tariffs on certain Canadian aluminum exports.
